A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Mono4DGS-HDR. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction comparisons and ablations on Syn-Exp-3, Real-Exp-3 and Real-Exp-2, including quantitative results and rendered examples.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds exposure robustness experiments, prior-loss ablations, convergence plots and qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: Sections 3 and A.1 retain the same two-stage Gaussian optimization, video-to-world transformation, motion representation and losses. The new ablations evaluate existing components; suggested RAW-domain, reflection and deblurring extensions are not implemented.

E1.justification: The same 25 scenes and three dataset groups remain. V2 extends evaluated conditions to nonperiodic/random exposures, inaccurate supplied exposure values and wider view changes (A.3.3–A.3.4). The challenging scenes discussed in A.4 already belong to the retained datasets.

E2.justification: GaussHDR, HDR-HexPlane, SplineGS-HDR, MoSca-HDR and GFlow-HDR retain their participation in the corresponding comparisons. The GFlow comparison moves from v1 Table 4 to v2 Table 5 unchanged; newly cited methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Existing splits, metrics, resolution and training budgets remain unchanged. Added protocols regenerate training LDR frames with shuffled/random exposures while retaining test exposures, perturb exposure inputs within ±0.25/0.5/0.75 EV, and separately remove depth or flow/track losses (Tables 6–8).

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands diagnostics with exposure-schedule robustness, exposure-error sensitivity, depth/flow supervision ablations, loss convergence, CRF recovery, wider-view examples and illustrated failures (Tables 6–8; Figures 11–15). The spline-control-point ablation already existed in v1 and is merely relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, standard deviations or statistical significance tests. V2's exposure perturbation ranges and loss curves describe sensitivity and convergence, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results remain unchanged, but substantial additional results appear. Tables 6–8 report HDR PSNR of 37.37/37.42 under randomized exposure conditions, 34.32 with ±0.75 EV exposure errors, and 35.56/35.05 without depth/flow-track losses, versus the retained full-model reference of 37.64. New plots and renderings also document convergence, CRF errors and failures.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(11), Gaussian and spline definitions, transformation reasoning, loss definitions and HDR-TAE formulation are retained. No new theorem, proof or substantive mathematical revision appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about the first unposed monocular 4D HDR system, two-stage optimization, temporal luminance regularization, benchmark and superior rendering quality/speed.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands applicability and mechanism discussion. It attributes exposure-related degradation to flow and CRF inaccuracies, qualifies wider-view evidence as qualitative without ground truth, and newly identifies complex non-rigid motion as an ARAP-related limitation. Sections A.4–A.5 also discuss challenging surfaces, lighting and illustrated failures beyond v1's shorter prior-quality and motion-blur limitations.

D1.justification: V2 explicitly identifies camera metadata as the exposure-value source and describes input generation for the new exposure experiments. Existing implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, project URL and conditional code/data release statement remain unchanged; the reproducibility statement moves to A.7.

R1.justification: V2 adds Mono-ViFI and Towards Better Data Exploitation in Self-Supervised Monocular Depth Estimation to the reprojection discussion, plus GaussianShader and TransparentGS as possible extensions for reflective/transparent surfaces. The main related-work narrative and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Existing prose remains largely unchanged. V2 moves the spline ablation and tracking discussion into Sections 4.3–4.4, relocates ethics/reproducibility/LLM statements to A.6–A.8, and adds acknowledgements, conference headers and appendix subsections.

P2.justification: Three new tables (6–8) and five new figures (11–15) substantially expand the visual presentation with robustness results, loss/CRF plots, wider views and failure examples. Existing displays are retained, including the spline table and tracking figure relocated into the main text.

improvement.justification: Tables 6–8 test previously unexamined exposure assumptions and prior dependence, while Figure 15 and the expanded limitations make failure conditions clearer. These provide a useful improvement in supporting validation and transparency. The principal comparisons remain unchanged, wider-view validation remains qualitative, and randomized experiments still lack repeated-run uncertainty.
